problem.title: Citrus Farming in Vale do Ribeira
problem.paragraph1: Every year, citrus growers lose part of their harvest without knowing why. Nutritional deficiency symptoms on the leaf are subtle, easily confused with diseases like greening (HLB), and an accurate diagnosis usually requires a specialist — who isn't always available when needed.
problem.paragraph2: During field research at Sítio São Miguel, we found a high incidence of manganese deficiency, cases of copper deficiency, and frequent signs of greening across the plantation.

cards.title: Confusion with Greening
cards.subtitle: Similar symptoms, different causes
cards.description: Manganese deficiency, copper deficiency, and greening all cause very similar spots and yellowing on the leaf — leading to wrong diagnoses and ineffective treatments.

cards.title: Late diagnosis
cards.subtitle: The damage is already done
cards.description: In most cases, the grower only notices the problem once the fruit has already been affected — and part of the harvest is already compromised.

cards.title: Technical difficulty
cards.subtitle: Specialized knowledge is scarce
cards.description: Correctly identifying the deficiency requires technical expertise that not every property has easy or quick access to.

project.name: Nitrusleaf
project.subtitle: AI-powered smart leaf diagnosis for citrus farming
project.description: A mobile app that uses computer vision and neural networks to identify nutritional deficiencies in mandarin leaves. The grower takes a photo of the leaf and gets an accurate diagnosis in seconds, right in the field.

header.title: How we built it
header.subtitle: From data collection to working prototype

fieldCollection.title: Data collection
fieldCollection.subtitle: Field Research
paragraphs: We conducted field research at Sítio São Miguel, in Pariquera-Açu/SP, to understand the real conditions of mandarin (Citrus reticulata) cultivation.
Through a structured questionnaire, we collected first-hand data on day-to-day crop management and gathered real leaf samples.
checklist: Real, hands-on learning about daily life in the orchard
A wide range of deficiency stages captured

preprocessing.title: Preprocessing and data augmentation
preprocessing.subtitle: Standardization and Data Augmentation
paragraphs: Images went through automatic orientation correction and were resized to 224 × 224 pixels, using proportional scaling with border padding to preserve their visual characteristics.

During training, we applied data augmentation exclusively to the training images, generating three synthetic variations per image through horizontal flips, rotation, and changes in saturation, brightness, and exposure.

training.title: Model training
training.subtitle: Convolutional Neural Network
paragraphs: We built a Convolutional Neural Network with three convolutional blocks, using 32, 64, and 128 filters, responsible for extracting visual features from the leaves at different levels of complexity.
The model uses a dense layer with 512 neurons and 50% Dropout. Training was performed with the Adam optimizer, binary crossentropy loss function, and Early Stopping with a patience of 10 epochs.
checklist: Early Stopping to select the best-performing model

validation.title: Validation
validation.subtitle: Model evaluation
paragraphs: After training, the model was evaluated on a test set of 25 images that were not used during training or validation.
The model achieved 95.97% accuracy on the test set, showing it can distinguish healthy leaves from leaves with manganese deficiency in unseen images.

prototype.title: Working prototype
prototype.subtitle: Mobile App
paragraphs: We built a mobile app capable of analyzing images of Citrus reticulata leaves and identifying signs of manganese deficiency using the AI model.
The solution was designed to give growers a fast, accessible preliminary diagnosis directly from their phone, based on a photo of the leaf.
checklist: App built exclusively for mobile devices
